tasks.details:
Follow docs/EXECUTION_PROVIDER.md. Validate working directories, filter environments, own spawned processes, enforce timeouts, terminate process groups, and stream stdout and stderr. Persist ordered events so reconnecting clients can continue from their last event position. Return exit status and support cancellation.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE:
- Created app/execution/ package: base.py (ExecutionProvider ABC), models.py (ExecutionContext/Process/ProcessEvent dataclasses + raw-SQL CRUD following app/projects/models.py pattern), host.py (HostExecutionProvider)
- Added SQLite tables in app/db.py: execution_contexts, processes, process_events (event id doubles as the reconnect position for stream_output(process_id, after_id))
- Working directory validated via existing validate_repository_path/ALLOWED_PROJECT_ROOTS
- Environment filtered to safe base allowlist (PATH/HOME/LANG/LC_ALL/TERM/TZ/USER/SHELL) plus explicit overrides, not full os.environ passthrough
- Processes spawned with start_new_session=True for process-group ownership
- Process termination: stop_process/timeout both terminate via SIGTERM then SIGKILL after grace period
- Fixed critical bug: grace-period liveness check now uses popen.poll() for immediate zombie detection instead of os.kill(pid,0) which succeeded on zombies, causing unnecessary 5s delays
- All tests passing: 10/10 existing suite + new test_execution.py covering success, failure exit code, cancellation, execution timeout, path-outside-allowed-roots rejection, and event-resume-from-position

Implemented per the approved plan (plan file: toasty-dreaming-torvalds.md). Summary of changes:

Schema: added terminal_sessions and terminal_events tables to app/db.py using idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS statements (no migration framework in this repo).

app/workspace/terminal_models.py: DB CRUD operations mirroring app/execution/models.py conventions with create/get/list/set_status/touch for sessions and add/list with after_id resume for events.

app/workspace/terminal.py: drives tmux entirely through one-shot CLI commands via ExecutionProvider.execute() (new-session, send-keys -l for literal text, send-keys with allowlisted control keys, pipe-pane -o to mirror pane output to file, has-session for liveness, kill-session). No PTY support added to HostExecutionProvider itself; tmux supplies the PTY. Module-level _TerminalManager (lock-guarded dict of daemon tailer threads) tails each session's pipe-pane output file and writes ANSI-stripped chunks into terminal_events. ensure_running() lazily restarts a tailer or marks a session LOST if the tmux server is gone after an AgentFlow restart; the tmux session itself survives because it's a separate OS process.

tasks.title: Fix 5 hardcoded Playwright UI tests to work without pre-started dev server
tasks.description: Repair 5 failing Playwright tests that hardcode http://127.0.0.1:5000 and require a manually-started Flask server, causing false failures in pytest runs without external setup. Make them self-contained by either spinning up an ephemeral Flask server fixture or guarding them with a skip check.
tasks.details:
Investigate why tests/test_chat_message.py::test_send_and_display_chat_message, tests/test_chat_message.py::test_chat_form_input_and_state, tests/test_codex_chat_response.py::test_codex_message_and_response, tests/test_hello_codex.py::test_send_hello_get_codex_response, and tests/test_hello_message.py::test_send_hello_message_via_ui were written against a live external server instead of using the Flask test client fixture pattern documented in CLAUDE.md.

Choose one of two approaches:

(a) Self-contained server fixture: Create a session-scoped pytest fixture (or conftest helper) that:
  - Spawns a Flask dev server in a subprocess using multiprocessing or threading
  - Binds to an ephemeral port (0) and discovers the assigned port
  - Passes the server URL (e.g., http://127.0.0.1:<dynamic-port>) to Playwright tests via pytest parametrization or indirect fixture injection
  - Tears down the server after the test session completes
  - Ensures the server is reachable before tests run (wait with retry/timeout)

(b) Skip guard (if integration with live server is essential):
  - Add a pytest skip check following the existing shutil.which(...) convention in CLAUDE.md
  - Create a helper function that attempts to connect to http://127.0.0.1:5000 with a short timeout (e.g., socket or requests.head)
  - Decorate each test with @pytest.mark.skipif(not is_server_reachable(), reason="Flask dev server not running on port 5000")
  - Ensure the skip is clean and does not report as a failure

Prefer approach (a) if Playwright automation and end-to-end UI verification are core to the test strategy; use (b) only if there is a genuine reason these tests must exercise a live running server rather than a fixture-managed one.

Update the hardcoded base URL references in all 5 tests to use the dynamically assigned URL (via fixture or conftest variable).
tasks.testStrategy:
Run pytest from a clean state with no pre-started Flask dev server on port 5000 and verify:
  1. All 5 tests pass (or skip cleanly if using approach b)
  2. No timeout errors or Page.wait_for_selector failures for #chatContainer
  3. Full pytest run reports 0 failures from these test files
  4. If using approach (a), confirm the ephemeral server is started before tests and cleaned up after
  5. If using approach (b), confirm tests skip gracefully and pytest exit code is 0
  6. Run pytest with -v to show each test result and confirm the expected behavior

tasks.description: Add documents and document_refs tables to the SQLite schema, extend agent_sessions with document tracking columns, and implement document CRUD helpers and dataclasses following existing app patterns.
tasks.details:
1. Extend app/db.py SCHEMA with two new tables:
   - documents: id (PK), project_id (FK), repo_id (FK), chain_id, doc_type [DESIGN|IMPLEMENTATION|TESTING|PLAN|STANDARD], path, title, status [DRAFT|IN_REVIEW|APPROVED|SUPERSEDED], current_git_sha, supersedes_id (self-FK, nullable), created_at, updated_at
   - document_refs: document_id (FK), referenced_document_id (FK), relationship [DERIVES_FROM|REFERENCES|SUPERSEDES], primary key (document_id, referenced_document_id)

2. Extend agent_sessions table with two new nullable columns:
   - document_id (FK to documents)
   - reviewed_git_sha

3. Add three new event_type values to agent_events (reuse existing table, no new table):
   - review_comment with data={line_start, line_end, body, severity}
   - review_verdict with data={verdict}
   - doc_read with data={document_id, git_sha}

4. Create app/documents/models.py following the pattern established in app/projects/models.py and app/agents/models.py:

5. Validate foreign key constraints and cascade behavior (e.g., deleting a document should handle document_refs appropriately per design intent).

6. This is data-layer only—no UI, no pipeline wiring, no review-loop automation per DOCUMENT_LIFECYCLE.md section 13.

Define YAML schema in app/pipelines/schema.py:
```yaml
pipeline:
  name: string
  version: string
  rigging:
    setup: [steps]
    teardown: [steps]
  steps:
    - name: string
      type: task | approval | subprocess | rigging
      config:
        if_type_task:
          task_id: string
          timeout: seconds
        if_type_approval:
          prompt: string
          required_approvers: [user_ids]
        if_type_subprocess:
          pipeline_ref: string
          params: {key: value}
      compensation:
        on_failure: retry | skip | abort | manual_review
        retry_count: integer
        retry_delay: seconds
    - name: string
      depends_on: [step_names] (optional)
```

   - Run: `pytest tests/test_backlog_sprint_viewports.py -v` at 375px and 1280px
   - Run: `pytest tests/ -k viewport -v` to execute all existing viewport tests
   - Verify all tests pass without skips or errors

2. Manual Real-Browser Exercises (Playwright):
   - Create tests/test_phase2_ui_verification.py with test functions for each page/viewport combination
   - For each Phase 2 page (backlog inbox, triage, sprint items, sprint planning, tasks review, readiness review, pipeline execution, Ralph execution, artifact library, acceptance criteria):
     - Launch browser at 375px viewport, navigate to page, interact with all controls (buttons, forms, modals, graphs), capture screenshot, verify no horizontal scrollbars, verify all text readable, verify touch targets accessible
     - Repeat at 1280px, verify layout differences (sidebar visible, graph left-to-right, etc.)
     - Use Playwright assertions: `expect(page).not_to_have_js_errors()`, `expect(locator).to_be_visible()`, `expect(locator).to_have_css('width', ...)` for touch targets

3. JavaScript Defect Verification:
   - Browser console: enable `console.error` and `console.warn` capture in Playwright, verify no uncaught exceptions
   - app.js: test AJAX submission on a backlog quick-add form, verify network request sent, row removed from DOM on success
   - pipeline.js: resize viewport during graph display, verify graph reflows, step click opens inspector without console errors
   - acceptance.js: load template, fill criteria form, submit, verify modal closes and list updates
   - Use Playwright `page.on('console')` to catch JavaScript errors: `assert no console.error messages found`

4. Assertions for Fixes:
   - For each defect fixed, add a test case that would have failed before the fix:
     - Touch target sizing: `expect(button).to_have_css('min-width', '44px')` or `expect(button_box.width).to_be_greater_than_or_equal(44)`
     - Horizontal scroll: `expect(page.viewport_size['width']).to_equal(375)` and `expect(document.body.scrollWidth).to_equal(document.body.clientWidth)`
     - Event handlers: trigger interaction (click, form submit), verify DOM mutation occurred (row removed, modal opened, status updated)
     - Graph reflow: capture graph dimensions at 375px and 1280px, verify height increases and width stays within viewport at 375px
   - Document each assertion in test with comment explaining the defect it guards against

5. Regression Testing:
   - Run full test suite: `pytest tests/ -v` after fixes to ensure no regressions
   - Run Playwright tests in headful mode: `pytest tests/test_phase2_ui_verification.py -v --headed` for visual inspection
   - Test on real mobile device or emulated device using Playwright device descriptors (iPhone 12, Pixel 5) to verify actual touch behavior

6. Sign-off Criteria:
   - All viewport tests pass at 375px and 1280px
   - No console errors in browser at either viewport
   - All Phase 2 pages load and are interactive without horizontal scrollbars at 375px
   - Touch targets (buttons, form inputs, interactive elements) are ≥44px and easily tappable
   - Graphs, tables, and modals render correctly at both viewports
   - JavaScript interactions (form submit, AJAX, modal open/close, graph navigation) work without errors
   - At least 5 defects identified and fixed with corresponding test assertions added
   - All fixes committed with clear messages and no regressions in existing tests

tasks.title: Page replay event loading: Implement paged/incremental event loading with checkpointed seeks
tasks.description: Optimize Replayer to load pipeline_events incrementally with pagination instead of reading all events on every request, keeping checkpointed seeks for 100k+ event logs to remain performant.
tasks.details:
Modify app/pipelines/replay.py to implement paged event loading:

1. Extend Replayer class with checkpoint-based pagination:
   - Add load_events_page(run_id, page_size=1000, checkpoint_offset=None) that returns events from checkpoint forward
   - Implement checkpoint_at_event(event_number) to save (event_number, reconstructed_state) pairs every K events (e.g., K=5000)
   - Store checkpoints in memory during replay session or in a replay_checkpoints table (run_id, checkpoint_number, event_offset, state_json)

2. Update ReplayController to manage pagination:
   - Fetch events in page_size chunks rather than all at once
   - Use nearest checkpoint to seek forward (e.g., jump to checkpoint 50k, then load 1000-event pages)
   - Track current page position and total event count
   - Implement has_next_page()/has_prev_page() for UI controls

3. Modify timeline reconstruction:
   - When seeking to event N, find nearest checkpoint <= N, reconstruct from checkpoint, then replay remaining events up to N
   - This converts O(total_events) reconstruction to O(K + remaining_events) where K is checkpoint interval
   - Keep memory footprint constant by not holding all events in RAM

4. API changes:
   - GET /executions/<id>/replay/events?page=1&page_size=1000 returns paginated events + checkpoint metadata
   - GET /executions/<id>/replay/seek?event_num=50000 uses checkpoint to jump efficiently
   - Response includes total_events, current_page, next_page_available for UI pagination controls

5. Frontend (static/pipeline.js):
   - Implement lazy event loading in timeline: fetch pages as user scrolls
   - Show loading indicator while fetching next page
   - Cache loaded pages in memory to avoid re-fetching
   - Display event count and current page info

When promote_next() is called and the lock cannot be acquired, enqueue the sprint/task with wait=True instead of failing. Create project_lock_queue table tracking waiter (sprint_id, task_id), priority, queued_at. Implement wait_for_lock() that blocks until the lock is released and the waiter is at queue head. Update RalphOrchestrator to use wait_for_lock() for automatic mode runs.

Document the decision in RUN_AND_RALPH §22. If read-only: add is_read_only property to terminal context that checks active locks, display warning banner in terminal UI. 5. **Heartbeat and cleanup**: Ensure heartbeat thread in lock.py refreshes locks held by active processes. Add reconcile logic at app startup to release orphaned locks, promote waiting queue entries when locks are freed, and handle stale lock takeover according to timeout rules.

Web queries built from question and library names only, with reports indicating which layer each finding came from.
tasks.details:
1. **Web fetcher abstraction and web_cache table** (app/agents/base.py, app/agents/models.py):
   - Define WebFetcher ABC in app/agents/base.py with methods: search(query, max_results=10) → list of {url, title, snippet, relevance_score}, fetch(url) → {url, content, content_hash, mime_type}, and cache_check(url, kind='web_content') → cached entry or None
   - Create HostWebFetcher in app/agents/host.py using requests and BeautifulSoup for HTML parsing; raise SecurityError if URL matches AGENTFLOW_BLOCKED_DOMAINS or contains disallowed schemes (file://, etc.)
   - Add web_cache table to app/agents/models.py: id, url, content_hash, content_excerpt (first 500 chars), fetched_at, expires_at (computed by kind: web_content=7 days, web_search_result=30 days), kind, source_session_id, is_stale (boolean), stale_refresh_requested (boolean)
   - Implement CacheEntry model with refresh(force=False) method: if is_stale or force, re-fetch and update expires_at, content_hash, fetched_at; else return cached

2. **RESEARCH session extension** (app/agents/base.py research() method):
   - After loading repository and knowledge base context (Phase A), if web_search_enabled=True in session config, build search queries from: (a) the research question split into keywords, (b) library entry titles and tags
   - Call fetcher.search(query) for each constructed query, dedup by URL
   - For each unique URL, call fetcher.fetch(url) and check cache first via cache_check(url)
   - If cached and not stale, use cached entry; if stale or not cached, fetch and store new web_cache entry with source_session_id
   - Limit total fetches to cost_limit_usd converted to approximate fetch count (e.g., 100 fetches ≈ $0.10)
   - Return findings_by_layer dict: {"repository": [...], "knowledge_base": [...], "web_search": [...], "web_fetch": [...]}, each with source URL, content snippet, and layer name

3. **Query builder from context** (app/agents/research_query_builder.py, new):
   - Implement build_search_queries(question, library_entries, max_queries=5) → list of strings
   - Extract keywords from question using simple stemming (Porter or nltk)
   - For each knowledge base entry in library_entries, extract title keywords and top tags
   - Combine related keywords into 2-3 word queries avoiding duplicates
   - Return top 5 by relevance heuristic (TF-IDF or keyword overlap)

4. **Report enhancement** (app/agents/models.py ResearchResult):
   - Extend findings_summary JSON to include layer_breakdown: {"repository_findings": int, "knowledge_base_findings": int, "web_search_results": int, "web_content_fetches": int}
   - Add findings_by_layer to persisted research_report: list of {source_layer, title, url, content_excerpt, confidence, fetched_at}
   - In HTML/JSON report output, group findings by layer with visual separator or heading

5. **Stale cache refresh on demand** (app/agents/models.py, web_cache endpoints):
   - Add refresh_cache endpoint (POST /api/research/web-cache/<cache_id>/refresh) that sets stale_refresh_requested=True
   - On next RESEARCH session using that cache entry, detect flag and force refresh if enabled
   - Log refresh action with timestamp in web_cache.updated_at and metadata

6. **Security and rate limiting**:
   - Validate all URLs against AGENTFLOW_BLOCKED_DOMAINS (default: ["localhost", "127.0.0.1", "*.internal"])
   - Implement token-bucket rate limiter for fetches: default 10 fetches per minute per session
   - Redact sensitive patterns (AGENTFLOW_REDACT_PATTERNS) from fetched content before storage
   - Log fetch count and cost per session

tasks.title: Design agent capability delivery: compare skill files vs MCP server vs prompt injection
tasks.description: Conduct a design discussion to determine how agents access the research knowledge base and extended capabilities. Compare three architectural approaches: (a) per-agent skill/instruction files, (b) AgentFlow-hosted MCP tool server, (c) prompt library and context injection. Output a decision recorded in AGENT_ADAPTER section 23.1 with follow-up implementation tasks.
tasks.details:
This is a design-phase task requiring no code implementation, only a structured analysis and decision record.

1. **Enumerate the three approaches and their trade-offs**:
   - **(a) Per-agent skill files** (SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc.): Agents discover adapter-specific instructions at runtime, similar to CloudCLI. Trade-offs: adapter-specific knowledge lives outside AgentFlow; testability requires each adapter to parse and follow custom formats; token cost varies by agent.
   - **(b) AgentFlow MCP server**: AgentFlow exposes research and other capabilities as an MCP tool server. Agents call tools via a uniform interface. Trade-offs: all agents gain uniform access; requires MCP client support in each agent; adds latency for tool calls; centralized cost control.
   - **(c) Prompt library injection**: AgentFlow assembles effective prompts including knowledge, context files, and steering via the prompt library (task 30). Skills become unnecessary; behaviour is specified entirely in prompts. Trade-offs: maximal token cost upfront; full control over effective prompts recorded in execution_prompts; works equally well in interactive and pipeline sessions; simplest adapter design (no agent-specific logic).

2. **Evaluate against key criteria**:
   - *Adapter uniformity*: AGENT_ADAPTER.md section 11 states nothing outside an adapter depends on agent-specific behaviour. Assess which approach best isolates agent-specifics to the adapter implementation.
   - *FakeAgent testability*: FakeAgentAdapter (app/agents/fake.py) is driven by a scripted list of steps. Which approach best supports deterministic testing without external dependencies?
   - *Token cost*: Compare steady-state token consumption for interactive and pipeline (Ralph) sessions. Consider whether research knowledge must be injected per-prompt or can be cached/reused.
   - *Recorded effective prompts*: task 30 (execution_prompts) records the exact prompt sent to the agent. Which approach yields the most useful recorded prompts for debugging and compliance?
   - *Redaction*: app/runs/security.py applies secret redaction before persistence. How does each approach interact with redaction (e.g., are skill files redacted, are MCP tool responses redacted)?
   - *Interactive vs pipeline sessions*: Interactive agent sessions (app/sessions/) and Ralph runs (app/ralph/) have different latency requirements. Which approach scales better for both?

3. **Consult existing code and design documents**:
   - Review AGENT_ADAPTER.md (especially sections 11, 13, 22) for adapter contract and context assumptions.
   - Review app/prompts/models.py and app/prompts/defaults.py (from task 30) to understand prompt assembly infrastructure.
   - Review app/agents/codex.py, app/agents/base.py (AgentAdapter ABC) for current adapter structure.
   - Review docs/EXECUTION_PROVIDER.md section 13 (agent context and steering) for how adapters currently receive guidance.
   - Check whether task 34 (project context files, CLAUDE.md discovery) influences the design.

4. **Identify and document open questions**:
   - Should skill files be stored in the project root (e.g., ./.agents/CLAUDE.md) or in AgentFlow (e.g., app/agents/skills/)?
   - If using MCP, should AgentFlow host the server in-process or as a subprocess?
   - Should the research knowledge base be queried on-demand (slower, lower cost per-session) or preloaded into the prompt (higher upfront cost, simpler agent interaction)?
   - How should agents signal when they need research capabilities (e.g., a research mode flag, or automatic detection)?

5. **Record the decision**:
   - Write a decision record in docs/AGENT_ADAPTER.md under a new section 23.1 titled "Agent Capability Delivery Architecture".
   - Include the selected approach, rationale (which criteria were most important and why), and a summary of trade-offs accepted.
   - Note any constraints (e.g., if MCP support is missing in a key agent, fall back to prompt injection for that agent).
   - List follow-up tasks to implement the decision (e.g., "Implement MCP server for research", "Add research knowledge to prompt library", etc.).

6. **Generate follow-up tasks**:
   - For each approach element that was chosen, create a task (or mark as deferred). For example:
     - If prompt injection is selected: create task "Inject research knowledge and extended context into agent prompts via task 30 prompt library" and "Record effective prompts for all agent sessions and runs".
     - If MCP server is chosen: create task "Implement AgentFlow MCP server for research and tool access" and "Add MCP client support to CodexAdapter (or other adapters)".
     - If skill files are chosen: create tasks for each adapter (e.g., "Create SKILL.md for CodexAdapter", "Create SKILL.md for FakeAgentAdapter").
tasks.testStrategy:
This is a design task; verification involves documentation and decision traceability, not unit tests:

1. **Decision documentation**:
   - Confirm docs/AGENT_ADAPTER.md section 23.1 exists and is properly formatted (title, approach, rationale, trade-offs, constraints).
   - Verify the decision is justified against all five criteria (adapter uniformity, FakeAgent testability, token cost, recorded prompts, interactive vs pipeline).
   - Check that the decision does not contradict existing architecture (e.g., does not violate AGENT_ADAPTER section 11 on adapter uniformity).

3. **Stakeholder review** (if applicable):

   - Confirm no open questions remain unaddressed in the document (list deferred items explicitly if necessary).

4. **Consistency check**:
   - Verify the chosen approach is compatible with tasks 30 (prompt library) and 34 (project context files).
   - Check that the decision does not create new dependencies on unimplemented external tools (e.g., if MCP is chosen, confirm agents support MCP or add that as a blocker).

tasks.details:
Implement skill management as an extension of app/prompts/ (task 30), NOT as a separate app/skills/ module, per docs/AGENT_ADAPTER.md section 23.3:

1. **Data Model Extension** (app/prompts/models.py):
   - Add columns to prompt_fragments table:
     - skill_status: enum('draft', 'active', 'deprecated', NULL) — NULL = not a skill
     - skill_when_to_use: text (markdown guidance)
     - skill_constraints: JSON array (advisory list, not machine-evaluated DSL)
     - skill_depends_on: JSON array of skill fragment IDs (cycle-checked)
     - skill_roles: JSON array (GENERAL/PLANNING/IMPLEMENTATION/RESEARCH/VERIFICATION from app/agents/base.py AGENT_ROLES tuple)
     - skill_adapter_types: JSON array (e.g., ['codex', 'claude']; empty = applies to all)
     - skill_priority: integer (order of inclusion in prompts)
     - skill_author: text
   - Add changelog column to prompt_fragment_versions table
   - Add AGENT_ROLES = ('GENERAL', 'PLANNING', 'IMPLEMENTATION', 'RESEARCH', 'VERIFICATION') tuple to app/agents/base.py

2. **Skill Management Functions** (app/prompts/models.py):
   - list_skills(db, role=None, agent_type=None, status='active') → list of skill fragments
   - resolve_skill_order(skills: list) → topologically sorted + priority-ordered list (cycle detection)
   - validate_skill(db, skill_fragment) → validate schema, check dependencies exist, return errors or None
   - deprecate_skill(db, skill_id, reason=None) → mark as deprecated, archive references
   - _check_skill_dependencies(db, skill_id, visited=set()) → recursive cycle detection

3. **Skill Assembly & Prompt Injection** (app/prompts/assembler.py):
   - skill_context(db, role, agent_type, project_id) → (formatted_text, skill_names) or (empty, []) on error
   - Never raises; logs warning and degrades gracefully per section 23.2 fallback requirement
   - Wired into assemble_effective_prompt(db, name, role=None, agent_type=None, project_id=None) as optional params
   - Called from all prompt-building sites:
     - app/pipelines/engine.py: AGENT steps (pass role, adapter type from step definition)
     - app/ralph/orchestrator.py: iterations (IMPLEMENTATION role)
     - app/sprints/planning_agent.py: PlanningAgent accepts optional db, injects PLANNING-role skills
     - app/sessions/routes.py: interactive chat session start (previously never touched library; inject user's role or GENERAL)

4. **Placeholder Matching Fix** (app/agents/models.py):
   - AgentSession.title derivation: change from exact-match to .endswith() so skill-prefixed prompts don't become auto-derived titles

5. **Disk Mirror / Sync Strategy** (app/prompts/skill_sync.py):
   - SkillSyncer class: mirror skills as JSON (NOT YAML) under app/agents/skills/{adapter_type_or_generic}/ at startup
   - Idempotent seeding like seed_defaults; database remains source of truth
   - Syncing into project repos explicitly deferred (open follow-up task per section 23.2)
   - Called at app startup via extension initialization

6. **UI** (app/prompts/views.py + templates):
   - Add routes under existing prompts blueprint at /prompts/skills:
     - GET /prompts/skills: list all skills with filtering by role, adapter_type, status
     - GET /prompts/skills/create: form to create new skill
     - POST /prompts/skills: create skill (same AJAX _reply() convention as fragments/templates/blocks)
     - GET /prompts/skills/<id>: view/edit skill form
     - PATCH /prompts/skills/<id>: update skill metadata or mark deprecated
     - POST /prompts/skills/<id>/validate: validate skill schema and dependencies
   - No separate public REST API; no admin-only gate (app has no auth)
   - Templates reuse existing app/templates/prompts/ layout

7. **Fallback & Resilience**:
   - skill_context() never raises; returns empty tuple on database unavailability or validation error
   - Graceful degradation: log warning but continue execution
   - Constraint evaluation: advisory only; evaluate at session start and warn if unsatisfiable (e.g., network requirement)
   - Version pinning: allow sessions to request specific prompt_fragment_version.id

tasks.details:
Implement a comprehensive skill library and governance system following the architectural decision from task 51:

1. **Skill Definitions** (app/skills/definitions/ directory):
   - Create JSON/YAML skill definitions for each category:
     - Research skills: web_search_strategy.json (patterns for effective search queries, source validation, knowledge base integration), knowledge_base_query.json (structured querying of existing project knowledge), source_credibility_assessment.json (evaluating source reliability)
     - Testing skills: web_ui_testing.json (Playwright/Selenium patterns, viewport handling, accessibility), api_testing.json (REST/GraphQL patterns, payload construction, error handling), unit_test_patterns.json (mocking, fixtures, assertion patterns), framework_patterns.json (pytest, Jest, pytest-asyncio patterns)

     - Ralph debugging skills: failure_analysis_pattern.json (log examination, error categorization), retry_strategy.json (exponential backoff, idempotency), state_recovery.json (manual intervention points)

   Each skill file includes: title, description, when_to_use (decision criteria), constraints (limitations), dependencies (prerequisite skills), examples (3+ code/prompt examples), validation_rules (what makes successful application)

tasks.title: Fix follow-up issues from RESEARCH agent and skill management implementation
tasks.description: Address five critical issues surfaced during tasks 41/43-45/47/48/52-55: local model support in pipeline AGENT steps, research report redaction, cost limit enforcement, deferred web research tasks, and potential test flakiness in lock scopes.
tasks.details:
1. **Local model support in pipeline AGENT steps** (app/pipelines/manager.py and app/pipelines/engine.py):
   - Currently app/pipelines/manager.py's default_agent_factory branches on 'claude' for planning-role sessions but local catalog entries are unhandled for generic pipeline AGENT elements
   - Problem: app/pipelines/engine.py's _h_agent does not thread a resolved model onto the AgentContext it builds, so local-model support only works for sprint planning agent, not generic pipeline AGENT steps
   - Solution: Extend _h_agent() to accept and apply model_overrides (base_url, api_key) when instantiating AgentContext for local models; update default_agent_factory to resolve local catalog entries and pass them through; ensure ClaudeAdapter respects ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN for local models

2. **Research report redaction** (app/agents/research_agent.py):
   - ResearchAgent does not redact research_report content before storage, unlike other persisted agent output (app/runs/security.py redacts Run commands/logs/replies)
   - Required before task 43/44/48 wire research reports into Artifact Library or knowledge base
   - Solution: Apply app/runs/security.py's redaction pipeline to ResearchAgent.store_report() before writing to database; add test to verify sensitive patterns are masked in stored research artifacts

3. **Research cost limit enforcement** (app/agents/research_agent.py):
   - ResearchAgent.cost_limit_usd is recorded but not enforced because no dollar-per-token rate table exists
   - Cost limiting only works when an adapter directly reports a real cost_usd figure
   - Solution: Create a cost_calculator module (app/agents/cost_calculator.py) with per-provider token-to-cost rates (OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity, etc.); update ResearchAgent to track cumulative_cost_usd and raise CostLimitExceeded before token budget is exhausted; wire into research session resumption logic

4. **Deferred web research tasks** (tasks 49-50 context):
   - Tasks 49 (web research feeding knowledge base) and 50 (knowledge base wiki indexing) were deliberately deferred because both depend on task 48 (knowledge base persistence) landing first
   - These are the least-specified pieces of the RESEARCH cluster
   - Solution: Document deferral rationale in task backlog with explicit dependency link to task 48; mark as blocked until task 48 is completed; ensure task 48 completion unblocks task 49/50 in the workflow system

5. **Flaky lock scope test** (tests/projects/test_lock_scopes.py):
   - test_a_waiting_run_starts_after_the_holder_finishes shows occasional sqlite 'database is locked' error under concurrent test/agent activity in a shared working tree
   - Passes on isolated rerun, suggesting environmental concurrency issue rather than logic regression
   - Solution: Add test isolation: use separate temporary databases for concurrent test sessions; increase SQLite busy_timeout in test conftest; add explicit synchronization barriers between Heartbeat thread and test assertions; consider switching to pytest-xfail with flaky marker if issue is truly environmental; add logging to capture timing of lock acquisition/release when flaky state occurs
